en.greeting: Hi! Today we polish three small things that make a big difference: the -s at the end of words, short forms like I'm and don't, and the melody of questions. Say everything out loud as we go.

steps.title: Don't drop the -s
steps.text: Let's start with the little -s at the end of words. Tap each word to hear it.
steps.body: In Indonesian, words don't change. In English the **-s** is a real sound: it tells people **he/she/it** (*she works*) or **more than one** (*two books*). So always say it. After **p, t, k, f** it's a quiet **/s/** (no buzz in your throat). After a **vowel** or a buzzing sound like **b, d, g, l, m, n, v** it's **/z/**. Put a hand on your throat to feel the difference.

steps.title: Listen: one or more?
steps.text: Press play and listen to the very end of the last word.

question.prompt: Listen. Which word do you hear?
question.explanation: You heard **cats**, with a clear /s/ at the end: more than one cat. Both words fit the sentence, so only the final **-s** tells you the answer. That's why you must say it too.

steps.title: The extra syllable
steps.text: Some words get a whole extra syllable when you add -s.
steps.body: After **s, z, sh, ch, x** and a **j** sound (often spelled *ge*), the ending is **/ɪz/** and the word gets **one more syllable**: *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**. Look at the last **sound**, not the spelling: *goes* and *does* end in -es but have **no** extra syllable. And don't add one where it doesn't belong: *works* is one syllable, not *work-es*.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think about the last sound of the base verb.

question.prompt: Budi ___ TV every evening. How do you say the verb?
question.explanation: **watch** ends with **ch**, so the -es adds a syllable: **WATCH-iz**. 'watch' with no ending drops the he/she -s, and 'watch-s' squeezes the ending into one syllable. Both are common mistakes.

steps.title: -s in daily life
steps.text: Listen to each sentence, then say it yourself. Watch the end of every verb.
steps.body: Each sentence has a different -s: **/s/** (cooks, stops), **/z/** (plays, lives) or the extra syllable **/ɪz/** (washes).

examples.id: Rina main bulu tangkis setiap hari Minggu.

examples.en: My brother washes his car on Saturdays.
examples.id: Kakakku mencuci mobilnya setiap hari Sabtu.

examples.en: The bus stops near the market.

steps.title: Short forms
steps.text: Now the short forms we use all the time in conversation.
steps.body: We join small words: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**. **I'm** is one syllable that rhymes with *time*. **isn't** is **IZ-nt** and **doesn't** is **DUZ-nt**. **don't** has the *o* of *go*. The **n't** means *not*, so say the **n** clearly, or people may hear the opposite.

pairs.id: tidak (do not) · o seperti di go

steps.title: Listen for n't
steps.text: Listen carefully for the short form: is the sentence positive or negative?

question.listen: Budi isn't at the office today.
question.prompt: Listen. Is Budi at the office today?
question.explanation: You heard **isn't** (IZ-nt): *Budi isn't at the office today.* The **n't** makes it negative, so the answer is **No, he isn't.** If the speaker dropped the n, you would hear the opposite.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now build a sentence with a short form, then say it out loud: DUZ-nt.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Kakak perempuanku tidak makan daging.
question.explanation: **My sister** = she, so the negative is **does not → doesn't**, followed by the base verb **eat** (no -s). Say it as one smooth phrase: *My sister DUZ-nt eat meat.*

steps.title: Questions: up or down?
steps.text: Last thing: the melody at the end of a question.
steps.body: **Yes/no questions** start with *Are, Is, Do, Does…* and **go up at the end ↗**. **Wh- questions** start with *What, Where, When, Who, How…* and **go down at the end ↘**. Many Indonesian speakers go up at the end of every question, because Indonesian questions often rise. Quick test: can you answer **yes** or **no**? Go up. Do you need information? Go down.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Look at the first word of each question.

question.prompt: Which question usually goes DOWN at the end?
question.explanation: **What does Sari do?** starts with **What**, so it's a wh- question: your voice goes **down** ↘. The other two start with **Is** and **Does**: they are yes/no questions, so they go **up** ↗.

steps.text: Everything from today on one page, to keep.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita memoles tiga hal kecil yang besar pengaruhnya: bunyi -s di akhir kata, bentuk singkat seperti I'm dan don't, serta nada pertanyaan. Ucapkan semuanya dengan suara keras sambil kita belajar.

steps.title: Jangan hilangkan -s
steps.text: Kita mulai dari -s kecil di akhir kata. Ketuk setiap kata untuk mendengarnya.
steps.body: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata tidak berubah. Dalam bahasa Inggris **-s** adalah bunyi nyata: ia menunjukkan **he/she/it** (*she works*) atau **lebih dari satu** (*two books*). Jadi selalu ucapkan. Sesudah **p, t, k, f** bunyinya **/s/** yang pelan (leher tidak bergetar). Sesudah **vokal** atau bunyi yang bergetar seperti **b, d, g, l, m, n, v** bunyinya **/z/**. Letakkan tangan di leher untuk merasakan bedanya.

steps.title: Dengar: satu atau lebih?
steps.text: Tekan play dan dengarkan bagian paling akhir dari kata terakhir.

question.prompt: Dengarkan. Kata mana yang kamu dengar?
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar **cats**, dengan /s/ yang jelas di akhir: lebih dari satu kucing. Kedua kata cocok di kalimat itu, jadi hanya **-s** di akhir yang menentukan jawabannya. Karena itu kamu juga harus mengucapkannya.

steps.title: Suku kata tambahan
steps.text: Beberapa kata mendapat satu suku kata utuh saat diberi -s.
steps.body: Sesudah **s, z, sh, ch, x** dan bunyi **j** (sering ditulis *ge*), akhirannya **/ɪz/** dan katanya mendapat **satu suku kata tambahan**: *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**. Perhatikan **bunyi** terakhir, bukan ejaannya: *goes* dan *does* berakhiran -es tapi **tidak** punya suku kata tambahan. Jangan juga menambahkannya di tempat yang salah: *works* satu suku kata, bukan *work-es*.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pikirkan bunyi terakhir dari kata kerja dasarnya.

question.prompt: Budi ___ TV every evening. Bagaimana kamu mengucapkan kata kerjanya?
question.explanation: **watch** berakhir dengan **ch**, jadi -es menambah satu suku kata: **WATCH-iz**. 'watch' tanpa akhiran menghilangkan -s untuk he/she, dan 'watch-s' memampatkan akhirannya jadi satu suku kata. Keduanya kesalahan yang umum.

steps.title: -s dalam keseharian
steps.text: Dengarkan setiap kalimat, lalu ucapkan sendiri. Perhatikan akhir setiap kata kerja.
steps.body: Setiap kalimat punya -s yang berbeda: **/s/** (cooks, stops), **/z/** (plays, lives) atau suku kata tambahan **/ɪz/** (washes).

examples.id: Rina main bulu tangkis setiap hari Minggu.

examples.en: My brother washes his car on Saturdays.
examples.id: Kakakku mencuci mobilnya setiap hari Sabtu.

examples.en: The bus stops near the market.

steps.title: Bentuk singkat
steps.text: Sekarang bentuk singkat yang selalu kita pakai dalam percakapan.
steps.body: Kita menggabungkan kata-kata kecil: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**. **I'm** satu suku kata yang berima dengan *time*. **isn't** berbunyi **IZ-nt** dan **doesn't** berbunyi **DUZ-nt**. **don't** memakai bunyi *o* seperti di *go*. **n't** berarti *not* (tidak), jadi ucapkan **n**-nya dengan jelas, kalau tidak orang bisa mendengar kebalikannya.

pairs.id: tidak (do not) · o seperti di go

steps.title: Dengarkan n't
steps.text: Dengarkan bentuk singkatnya baik-baik: kalimatnya positif atau negatif?

question.listen: Budi isn't at the office today.
question.prompt: Dengarkan. Apakah Budi ada di kantor hari ini?
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar **isn't** (IZ-nt): *Budi isn't at the office today.* **n't** membuatnya negatif, jadi jawabannya **No, he isn't.** Kalau pembicara menghilangkan n-nya, kamu akan mendengar kebalikannya.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang susun kalimat dengan bentuk singkat, lalu ucapkan dengan keras: DUZ-nt.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Kakak perempuanku tidak makan daging.
question.explanation: **My sister** = she, jadi bentuk negatifnya **does not → doesn't**, diikuti kata kerja dasar **eat** (tanpa -s). Ucapkan sebagai satu frasa yang lancar: *My sister DUZ-nt eat meat.*

steps.title: Pertanyaan: naik atau turun?
steps.text: Terakhir: nada di akhir pertanyaan.
steps.body: **Pertanyaan yes/no** diawali *Are, Is, Do, Does…* dan **naik di akhir ↗**. **Pertanyaan wh-** diawali *What, Where, When, Who, How…* dan **turun di akhir ↘**. Banyak penutur Indonesia menaikkan nada di akhir setiap pertanyaan, karena pertanyaan bahasa Indonesia sering naik. Tes cepat: bisakah dijawab **yes** atau **no**? Naikkan. Butuh informasi? Turunkan.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Lihat kata pertama setiap pertanyaan.

question.prompt: Pertanyaan mana yang biasanya TURUN di akhir?
question.explanation: **What does Sari do?** diawali **What**, jadi ini pertanyaan wh-: suaramu **turun** ↘. Dua lainnya diawali **Is** dan **Does**: itu pertanyaan yes/no, jadi nadanya **naik** ↗.
